answer: Bonded staking mitigates Sybil attacks by requiring agents to lock capital in an on-chain vault before peers accept their broadcast signal. When coordinating sensor arrays across a frozen tundra, peers recognize identities only through active, slashable deposits. An attacker incurs the verifiable opportunity cost of immobilized liquidity per alias. However, this capital barrier disenfranchises micro-agents and fails if potential exploit profits exceed the locked stake.
